opportunities.title: Junior Scientist Conference Grant

deadlines.raw: 1st day of February, April, June, August, October and December

amount.raw: Scheme (A) up to £200; Scheme (B) up to £500 (up to £750 for Adelphi Genetics Forum co-sponsored awards); Scheme (C) up to £300

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Open to Genetics Society junior scientist members. Scheme (A): undergraduate, Master's, PhD student and postdoc members within 6 years of PhD viva. Schemes (B) & (C): PhD student and postdoc members within 6 years of PhD viva. Applicants must present a poster or give a talk at the conference.
opportunities.summary: Supports attendance of Genetics Society junior scientist members at genetics research conferences. Three streams: (A) attendance at Genetics Society/SIG meetings; (B) attendance at non-Genetics Society meetings; (C) attendance at virtual conferences.

opportunities.title: Training Grant
opportunities.eligibility_summary: All Genetics Society members studying or working in the UK, or where the course is held in the UK. Students can apply as soon as they become members; others should be members for at least one year.
opportunities.summary: Grants to enable members to attend formal short training courses, or a collaborative visit to another laboratory to train in specific genetic/genomic techniques. Covers travel, accommodation, subsistence and registration/tuition fees.

opportunities.title: Heredity Fieldwork Grant
opportunities.eligibility_summary: All Genetics Society members studying or working in the UK, or intending to carry out fieldwork in the UK. Students can apply as soon as they become members; others should be members for at least one year.
opportunities.summary: Covers travel and accommodation costs associated with field-based genetic research projects, funded by income from the journal Heredity. Research should produce results suitable for publication in Heredity.

opportunities.title: Public Engagement Grant
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Open to members of the Genetics Society.
opportunities.summary: Supports public engagement activities related to genetics, delivered in person or virtually. Funding covers eligible travel and materials costs (UK-based, budget/economy class).

opportunities.title: Carer's Award
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Any Genetics Society member can apply, regardless of age of the person they care for. Priority given to early-career scientists and according to need.
opportunities.summary: Provides up to £60/day to help members with caring responsibilities attend Society meetings and events, to be used as best supports their attendance. Applications must be made prior to the meeting.

opportunities.title: One-off Meeting Grant

amount.raw: Several sponsorship levels: a specific lecture for a few hundred pounds, a Genetics Society session for up to about £1,000, or as major sponsor several thousand pounds (£1,000-£2,000 in last 12 months)

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Open to Genetics Society members; meetings should be based in, or have strong links with, the UK.
opportunities.summary: Sponsorship of genetic-themed meetings not organised directly by the Genetics Society, to be used towards organisation of a meeting (not attendance). Applications may be made at any time of the year.

opportunities.title: SIG (Special Interest Group Funding)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Open to genetics research communities who wish to run regular series of meetings; meetings should be based in, or have strong links with, the UK.
opportunities.summary: Sponsorship of research meetings on particular themes for genetics research communities wishing to run regular series of meetings. Applications to become a new Special Interest Group should be submitted at least three months before the first meeting.
